notes: Subsystem schema versions are independent from the whole-game envelope schema.
A subsystem may be explicitly transient/non-saveable or an acknowledged gap; both states are machine-readable.

subsystems.rationale: Manual/autosave snapshots must pass semantic preflight before any primary replacement or autosave rotation can displace known-good disk state.

subsystems.snapshot: existing primary/backup save envelope schema inspection before write
subsystems.restore: preservation-only; newer save is not loaded by older schema
subsystems.rationale: A downgraded build must not overwrite newer-schema persistent player data. Whole-game saves require integrity-valid future envelopes; settings/input sidecars require parseable future envelopes with the expected payload container. A slot with a newer primary and an older valid backup may load the older backup, but remains explicitly future-protected and non-writable. Manual saves fail closed, autosave rotation skips protected slots, and sidecar writes fail closed without destructive mutation.

subsystems.snapshot: previous primary preserved as `.bak` before overwrite (NW.js file or browser localStorage generation)
subsystems.validator: backup must independently pass envelope integrity/migration and the same prepareSaveEnvelopeForApply semantic preflight as primary
subsystems.rationale: Malformed, checksum-invalid, migration-invalid, missing, or semantically unloadable primaries may recover the previous `.bak` generation only when that backup independently passes integrity/migration and full semantic preflight. Backup-only slots remain discoverable by listing and Continue; recovery provenance and the primary failure reason remain machine-visible. Manual overwrite and autosave rotation preserve the validated backup whenever the selected existing candidate came from `.bak`, so a known-bad primary cannot displace the only recoverable generation. Desktop and browser persistence share this recovery contract.

subsystems.validator: prepareSaveEnvelopeForApply semantic preflight + rollback fault-injection coverage
subsystems.rationale: A valid save may still encounter a late runtime exception during rehydration. Load application snapshots canonical live state before mutation and restores party, quest, world, runtime, and air-navigation state if any apply stage fails. Success markers are written only after apply commits; failed/rolled-back loads clear stale success evidence and preserve the original error plus rollback outcome. If rollback itself fails, loading fails closed with combined evidence.
Opening state is authored/transient; autosave occurs after stable chapter handoff.
Combat is not a resumable persistence boundary; autosave occurs after resolution.
Transient presentation state is not persisted directly.

subsystems.versionOwner: whole-game envelope schema + subsystem version owners
subsystems.rationale: Current bounded First Wake persistent world mutations are explicitly registered in docs/first-wake-persistent-mutations.json with snapshot, restore, semantic-validator, and version ownership. Unknown future persistent mutations are BLOCKING_UNREGISTERED until added to that registry. This does not implement deferred economy/crafting or relationship/private-action persistence.
No complete persistent economy/crafting contract is established yet.
Planned open-ended relationship/private-action state is not yet implemented as a persistence contract.

Accessibility and user preferences persist independently from game save slots. Missing/corrupt primaries recover from validated backup with explicit provenance; the first post-recovery edit preserves that backup while writing a new primary. Parseable newer-schema primary/backup sidecars are downgrade-protected from overwrite.

User control remaps persist independently from game saves and general accessibility settings. Missing/corrupt primaries recover from validated backup with explicit provenance; the first post-recovery edit preserves that backup while writing a new primary. Parseable newer-schema primary/backup sidecars are downgrade-protected from overwrite.
